questions.question: Container A ($V_A = 2\ \mathrm{L}$) holds gas at $P_A = 3\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. Container B ($V_B = 3\ \mathrm{L}$) holds gas at $P_B = 2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. A valve connects them. Find the final pressure (at the same temperature $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$).
questions.answer:
Total moles (conserved): $n_{\text{total}} = n_A + n_B = \dfrac{P_A V_A + P_B V_B}{RT}$

Final state: same $T$, total volume $V_A + V_B = 5\ \mathrm{L}$:

$P_f = \dfrac{n_{\text{total}} RT}{V_A + V_B} = \dfrac{P_A V_A + P_B V_B}{V_A + V_B}$

$= \dfrac{3\times10^5 \times 2 + 2\times10^5 \times 3}{5} = \dfrac{6\times10^5 + 6\times10^5}{5} = \dfrac{12\times10^5}{5} = 2.4\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

questions.question: Two containers hold the same gas. Container 1: $n_1 = 0.5\ \mathrm{mol}$, $T_1 = 400\ \mathrm{K}$, $V_1 = 5\ \mathrm{L}$. Container 2: $n_2 = 1\ \mathrm{mol}$, $T_2 = 200\ \mathrm{K}$, $V_2 = 5\ \mathrm{L}$. They are connected. Assuming no heat loss, find the final equilibrium temperature and pressure.
questions.answer:
**Temperature:** Energy is conserved (monatomic gas, $U = \frac{3}{2}nRT$):

$n_1 T_1 + n_2 T_2 = (n_1 + n_2)T_f$

$T_f = \dfrac{n_1 T_1 + n_2 T_2}{n_1 + n_2} = \dfrac{0.5 \times 400 + 1 \times 200}{1.5} = \dfrac{200 + 200}{1.5} = \dfrac{400}{1.5} \approx 266.7\ \mathrm{K}$

**Pressure:**

$P_f = \dfrac{(n_1 + n_2)RT_f}{V_1 + V_2} = \dfrac{1.5 \times 8.31 \times 266.7}{10\times10^{-3}} = \dfrac{3323.5}{0.01} = 3.32\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

questions.question: The general formula for the final pressure when two containers at the same temperature are connected is $P_f = (P_1 V_1 + P_2 V_2)/(V_1 + V_2)$. Derive this formula.
questions.answer:
Mole conservation: $n_f = n_1 + n_2$

$\dfrac{P_f(V_1+V_2)}{RT_f} = \dfrac{P_1 V_1}{RT_1} + \dfrac{P_2 V_2}{RT_2}$

When $T_1 = T_2 = T_f = T$ (isothermal connection):

$P_f(V_1+V_2)/T = P_1 V_1/T + P_2 V_2/T$

$P_f = \dfrac{P_1 V_1 + P_2 V_2}{V_1 + V_2}$ ✓

This is a weighted average of pressures, weighted by volume.

questions.question: Container A ($V = 4\ \mathrm{L}$, $P = 5\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$) is connected to an initially evacuated container B ($V = 6\ \mathrm{L}$, $P = 0$). Temperature stays constant. Find $P_f$.
questions.answer:
$P_f = \dfrac{P_A V_A + P_B V_B}{V_A + V_B} = \dfrac{5\times10^5 \times 4 + 0 \times 6}{4 + 6}$

$= \dfrac{20\times10^5}{10} = 2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

The gas expands isothermally into the vacuum. This is an example of free expansion — note that pressure drops by the ratio of original to total volume: $P_f = P_A \times V_A/(V_A + V_B) = 5\times10^5 \times 0.4 = 2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$.

questions.question: Three containers at the same temperature $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$ are connected: A ($V = 1\ \mathrm{L}$, $P = 6\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$), B ($V = 2\ \mathrm{L}$, $P = 3\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$), C ($V = 3\ \mathrm{L}$, $P = 1\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$). Find the final pressure.
questions.answer:
$P_f = \dfrac{P_A V_A + P_B V_B + P_C V_C}{V_A + V_B + V_C}$

$= \dfrac{6\times10^5 \times 1 + 3\times10^5 \times 2 + 1\times10^5 \times 3}{1 + 2 + 3}$

$= \dfrac{6 + 6 + 3}{6} \times 10^5 = \dfrac{15\times10^5}{6} = 2.5\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

questions.question: Container 1 ($V_1 = 3\ \mathrm{L}$, $T_1 = 600\ \mathrm{K}$, $P_1 = 2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$) and Container 2 ($V_2 = 3\ \mathrm{L}$, $T_2 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$, $P_2 = 1\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$) are connected (rigid, insulated walls except between containers). Find the equilibrium temperature $T_f$ for a monatomic ideal gas.
questions.answer:
Moles: $n_1 = P_1 V_1/(RT_1) = 2\times10^5 \times 3\times10^{-3}/(8.31 \times 600) = 600/4986 \approx 0.1203\ \mathrm{mol}$

$n_2 = P_2 V_2/(RT_2) = 1\times10^5 \times 3\times10^{-3}/(8.31 \times 300) = 300/2493 \approx 0.1203\ \mathrm{mol}$

Equal moles! Energy conservation:

$T_f = \dfrac{n_1 T_1 + n_2 T_2}{n_1 + n_2} = \dfrac{0.1203 \times 600 + 0.1203 \times 300}{2 \times 0.1203} = \dfrac{600 + 300}{2} = 450\ \mathrm{K}$

$P_f = \dfrac{(n_1+n_2)RT_f}{V_1+V_2} = \dfrac{0.2406 \times 8.31 \times 450}{6\times10^{-3}} = \dfrac{899.7}{6\times10^{-3}} \approx 1.5\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

questions.question: Two containers are connected by a tube with a closed valve. Left: $n_L = 2\ \mathrm{mol}$ at $T_L = 400\ \mathrm{K}$. Right: $n_R = 1\ \mathrm{mol}$ at $T_R = 100\ \mathrm{K}$. Both have volume $V$. After opening the valve (thermal equilibrium, monatomic ideal gas), find $T_f$.
questions.answer:
Energy conservation ($U = \frac{3}{2}nRT$):

$n_L T_L + n_R T_R = (n_L + n_R)T_f$

$T_f = \dfrac{n_L T_L + n_R T_R}{n_L + n_R} = \dfrac{2 \times 400 + 1 \times 100}{3} = \dfrac{800 + 100}{3} = \dfrac{900}{3} = 300\ \mathrm{K}$

The final temperature is the **mole-weighted average** of the initial temperatures.

questions.question: A gas-filled piston-cylinder (volume $V_1$, pressure $P_1$, temperature $T$) is connected to a rigid container (volume $V_2$, initially evacuated). The piston is free to move and maintains constant pressure $P_1$ throughout. Find the final volume of the cylinder after the gas expands.
questions.answer:
The gas expands at constant pressure $P_1$ until the total amount of gas fills both the cylinder (final volume $V_f$) and the container $V_2$.

Mole conservation (at temperature $T$, constant pressure $P_1$):

$n_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{P_1 V_1}{RT}$ (initially in cylinder)

Final state: cylinder volume $V_f$ (piston moved) + container $V_2$, all at pressure $P_1$:

$\dfrac{P_1(V_f + V_2)}{RT} = \dfrac{P_1 V_1}{RT}$

$V_f + V_2 = V_1 \Rightarrow V_f = V_1 - V_2$

The cylinder volume decreases by $V_2$ (gas flows into the container), and the total volume remains $V_1$.

questions.question: Container A holds $n_A = 3\ \mathrm{mol}$ of monatomic ideal gas at $T_A$. Container B holds $n_B = 1\ \mathrm{mol}$ at $T_B = 100\ \mathrm{K}$. After connecting (insulated rigid walls), the final temperature is $T_f = 325\ \mathrm{K}$. Find $T_A$.
questions.answer:
Energy conservation:

$n_A T_A + n_B T_B = (n_A + n_B)T_f$

$3 T_A + 1 \times 100 = 4 \times 325$

$3 T_A = 1300 - 100 = 1200$

$T_A = 400\ \mathrm{K}$

questions.question: Two containers A and B (both volume $V = 5\ \mathrm{L}$) hold helium. After connecting, the final state is $T_f = 300\ \mathrm{K}$, $P_f = 2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. Initially, container A was at $T_A = 500\ \mathrm{K}$ and container B at $T_B = 100\ \mathrm{K}$. Find the initial pressures $P_A$ and $P_B$.
questions.answer:
From conservation of energy:

$n_A T_A + n_B T_B = (n_A + n_B)T_f$

$n_A \times 500 + n_B \times 100 = (n_A + n_B) \times 300$

$500 n_A + 100 n_B = 300 n_A + 300 n_B$

$200 n_A = 200 n_B \Rightarrow n_A = n_B$

From mole conservation and final state:

$n_A + n_B = \dfrac{P_f \times 2V}{RT_f} = \dfrac{2\times10^5 \times 10\times10^{-3}}{8.31 \times 300} = \dfrac{2000}{2493} \approx 0.8023\ \mathrm{mol}$

$n_A = n_B = 0.4012\ \mathrm{mol}$

$P_A = \dfrac{n_A RT_A}{V} = \dfrac{0.4012 \times 8.31 \times 500}{5\times10^{-3}} = \dfrac{1665.8}{5\times10^{-3}} \approx 3.33\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

$P_B = \dfrac{n_B RT_B}{V} = \dfrac{0.4012 \times 8.31 \times 100}{5\times10^{-3}} \approx 0.667\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$
